messages.author: 595f772c619c0cb0
messages.subject: six-dimensional multidimensional IRT 2PL model - possible?
parts:
Greetings,

        New user of mIRT here. From the workshop examples and manual I understand that it is possible to fit a one-factor and two-factor model to the data using

unidim <- mirt(scored.data, 1)
multidim <- mirt(scored.data, 2)

       Is there a limitation to the number of factors I can use? I am interested in trying to get a and b parameters (2PL) according to a six factor model; can the mirt package practically handle this command?
multidim <- mirt(scored.data, 6)

Thanks in advance.

Sincerely,
Colin Wee
Graduate Student
University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: Re: six-dimensional multidimensional IRT 2PL model - possible?
parts:
Hi, Colin.

Why not? If your indicator variables can be explained by 6 latent variables theoretically, you can handle it. but, you have to change estimation method like this

mod1 <- mirt(scored.data, 6, method = 'QMCEM') or
mod2 <- mirt(scored.data, 6, method = 'MHRM')

Seongho
